title: Taifa of Valencia
capsule: The Taifa of Valencia was a Muslim principality in eastern al-Andalus that emerged from the collapse of the Córdoba Caliphate around 1010, governed by successive dynasties including the Amirids and later Slavic-origin rulers. It achieved international notoriety when the Castilian mercenary Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar (El Cid) captured Valencia in 1094 and ruled it personally until his death in 1099, after which his widow Jimena held the city until Almoravid pressure forced its abandonment and burning in 1102. Valencia was subsequently absorbed into the Almoravid empire, then passed through the second taifa period before Aragonese conquest under James I in 1238 definitively ended Islamic rule.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The taifa's general territorial extent in the Valencia region is attested, but its exact boundaries against neighboring taifas and the periods of El Cid's personal rule complicate precise cartographic representation.
